messages:
Maya: Heads-up — sketching a 'caretaker' UX for automatic-degrade liveness handoff. Want a quick brain dump before I lock the mock. Main goals: make the reason obvious, show liveness/KV staleness signals, and offer a safe operator takeover with TTL. @Liam @Ranjit PTAL

Maya: rough idea: show a compact card on rollout detail that says 'Degraded -> Caretaker' with 3 lines: reason, last health check, operator takeover button. Sample telemetry fields I think we need: `fallback_reason`, `kv_age_ms`, `last_success_ms`.

Liam: +1. Also surface an estimated recovery ETA based on historical restart patterns and current queue depth. :thumbsup:

Ranjit: Agree on explicit tags. One API question: should the router attach `fallback_reason` to every request or emit a separate event stream? I prefer attaching (for easy per-request debugging) but that may increase payload size.

Sasha: Quick product question — if KV cache is 'stale' do we do a soft degrade (token budget / conservative decoding) or immediate hard fallback to a smaller model? UX needs to explain the difference.

Maya: Prefer soft degrade when latency SLO is the constraint, hard fallback on persistent error-class spikes. Example thresholds I was thinking of:

```
# caretakers.config (sketch)
soft_degrade_when:
  - kv_age_ms > 3000
  - latency_p90 > 700ms
hard_fallback_when:
  - error_rate > 0.10 for >= 120s
```

Maya: The card would show which rule fired and a tiny line: "kv_age=3.5s · p90=820ms · errors=0.04" so operators get a quick read.

Nora: We need the audit side nailed: every takeover must be an auditable event with who clicked, TTL (auto-revert), and a generated event_id. Ops requires 7-day retention for these entries by default.

fallback-bot: Policy-sim run finished — 3/20 scenarios flagged for oscillation risk (short flapping between caretaker and primary). See /policy-sim/1764228888 for details.

Liam: That oscillation bit is important — UX should include a small 'oscillation risk' sparkline on the card and a quarantine toggle that prevents automatic re-enable for N minutes.

Ranjit: On the API side I still vote for explicit per-request tagting (`fallback_reason`) plus a separate event stream for higher-cardinality audit events. Console can index both.

Maya: Good call. We'll add both: per-request `fallback_reason` and an event stream for operator actions and policy-sim anomalies. Also adding `kv_age_ms` and `last_success_ms` to telemetry so we can display the exact numbers.

Sasha: UX nit — when operator clicks takeover, make the button read: `Take over for 15m ▾` with quick presets 15 / 60 / 240. Also show a one-click 'revert now' inline.

Nora: Confirmed. Also include a generated event id in the takeover modal and surface it in the audit log row for compliance.

Maya: I'll update the Figma mock and the RFC to reflect: explicit tags, double-stream telemetry, takeover presets, oscillation quarantine, and retention defaults. Linking the draft: https://www.figma.com/file/xxxxx/caretaker-ux (WIP) :sparkles: 

Liam: Thanks — can you also add a small sample of the per-request header we expect? e.g., `X-Fallback-Reason: kv_stale` so SDKs can plumb it through logs.

Maya: Yep, will add that to the RFC and the router PR. Will also include a tiny simulator to show oscillation risk before enabling auto-degrade. Thanks everyone!
